title: 7.1–7.3 Catch-Up

noticeAndWonder.context: Quick review from Lesson 7.3: Detective Park lines up 3 identical locked evidence boxes on a table. Together the 3 boxes hold 21 pieces of evidence, and each box holds the same amount. She writes 3x = 21 to find how many pieces are in each box.
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: (Review from 7.3) Apply: Evidence Boxes
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Park splits 96 pieces of evidence equally among several identical boxes. Each box ends up holding exactly 8 pieces. The equation 8b = 96 represents this situation, where b is the number of boxes. How many boxes did she use? Show your work using inverse operations.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Divide both sides of 8b = 96 by 8: b = 96 ÷ 8 = 12 boxes. Check: 8 × 12 = 96. ✓

turnAndTalk.question: Detective Park has 3 identical boxes holding 21 pieces of evidence total, written as 3x = 21. What does each part of the equation mean, and how is solving this different from solving x + 3 = 21?
turnAndTalk.kernel: In 3x = 21 the variable is multiplied, so I undo it with division.

stems.en: Solving 3x = 21 is different from x + 3 = 21 because ___.
stems.es: Resolver 3x = 21 es diferente de x + 3 = 21 porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students read 3x as 3 groups of x, recognize multiplication, and contrast it with addition, knowing they will divide (not subtract) to solve.
turnAndTalk.extend: Predict: would x in 3x = 21 be larger or smaller than in 5x = 21? Justify before solving.
extendStems: More boxes means each box has ___.

turnAndTalk.question: How did you undo the multiplication in 3x = 21 (or the division in x / 4 = 9) to isolate the variable?
turnAndTalk.kernel: I use the inverse operation: division undoes multiplication.

stems.en: I divided / multiplied both sides by ___, so the answer is ___.
stems.es: Dividí / multipliqué ambos lados por ___, así que la respuesta es ___.

stems.en: The inverse of ___ is ___, so I ___.
stems.es: El inverso de ___ es ___, así que ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students divide both sides by 3 to get x = 7 (or multiply by 4 to get x = 36) and name division/multiplication as inverse operations.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why does dividing only one side of 3x = 21 give the wrong answer? Compare doing it to one side versus both sides.
extendStems: Dividing only one side is wrong because ___.
To keep the equation true I must ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When would you solve a multiplication or division equation in real life?
turnAndTalk.kernel: These equations find an unknown when items are split into or made from equal groups.

stems.en: I would use this kind of equation to find ___.
stems.es: Usaría este tipo de ecuación para hallar ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students name a real context (equal price per item, sharing equally, total from groups) and choose the correct inverse operation to isolate the variable.
turnAndTalk.extend: Critique: 'To solve x / 5 = 12 you divide both sides by 5.' Explain the error and the correct inverse operation.
extendStems: This is wrong because the inverse of division is ___.
I should ___ both sides by 5, which gives ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Solve Multiplication and Division Equations, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Divide to undo multiplying, and multiply to undo dividing — always on both sides.

stems.en: I divided / multiplied both sides by ___, so the answer is ___.
stems.es: Dividí / multipliqué ambos lados por ___, así que la respuesta es ___.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.8 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate multiplied again instead of dividing to solve 6x = 42 (and got x = 252). How would you help them fix this common mistake? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equal sign showing both sides are the same.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática con un signo igual que muestra que ambos lados son iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: A math sentence that says two amounts are equal, with an = sign, is an ___.

examples.why: It has an equal sign showing two equal amounts.
That is an expression because it has no equal sign.

vocabulary.definitionVi: Một phát biểu toán học cho thấy hai biểu thức bằng nhau.
vocabulary.definitionAr: جملة رياضية تبين أن تعبيرين متساويان.

vocabulary.definition: A letter that stands for an unknown number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una letra que representa un número desconocido.
vocabulary.visual: In n + 3 = 10, the letter n stands for the unknown number (n = 7)

vocabulary.definitionAr: عملية تلغي تأثير عملية أخرى (مثل: الجمع والطرح).

vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar grupos iguales una y otra vez.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 7.1–7.3
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 7.1: Find the unknown, choose a variable, then turn the words into symbols around an equal sign. • 7.2: Undo the operation with its inverse, and do it to both sides to keep the equation balanced. • 7.3: Divide to undo multiplying, and multiply to undo dividing — always on both sides.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 7.1 — Write Equations: Find the unknown, choose a variable, then turn the words into symbols around an equal sign.
Lesson 7.2 — Solve One-Step Addition and Subtraction Equations: Undo the operation with its inverse, and do it to both sides to keep the equation balanced.
Lesson 7.3 — Solve Multiplication and Division Equations: Divide to undo multiplying, and multiply to undo dividing — always on both sides.

weDo.title: Quick guided checks — one from each lesson
lines: From 7.1: New clue: 'A number plus 5 equals 9.' What is the unknown?
From 7.2: Solve x − 4 = 9. Is x being added or subtracted?
From 7.3: Solve x ÷ 4 = 9. Is x multiplied or divided?

explore.instructions: Review from Lesson 7.3: Solve each equation by showing your work. Use inverse operations to isolate the variable.
hints: For multiplication equations like 3x = 21, the inverse is division. Divide both sides by the coefficient.
For division equations like x / 4 = 9, the inverse is multiplication. Multiply both sides by the divisor.
explore.label: Complete the table to solve each equation. Show your inverse operation and work.

discourse.prompt: How do you decide whether to multiply or divide to solve an equation?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When I see ___ in the equation, I know to ___ both sides because the inverse of ___ is ___.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.1) A witness statement reads: 'A number c of security cameras plus 6 more equals 19.' Which equation matches?
optional.explanation: 'Plus 6 more' means + 6 and 'equals 19' means = 19, so c + 6 = 19. Check: 13 + 6 = 19.
choiceFeedback: Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.

optional.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 − 7 = 8. Check: 8 + 7 = 15 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.3) Vault A is sealed with 4x = 32. Crack the lock: what is x?
optional.explanation: The 4 is multiplying x, so divide both sides by 4: x = 32 / 4 = 8. Check: 4 x 8 = 32.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.1) Which equation represents: 'A number plus 12 equals 30'?
approaching.explanation: 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + 12 = 30.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.
hints: Find the operation word in the sentence. What does 'plus' tell you to do with the number and 12?
Let n stand for the unknown number, then translate each phrase into symbols: 'a number' becomes n, 'plus 12' names an operation, 'equals 30' becomes = 30.
Build it left to right: n, then the symbol for 'plus', then 12, then '= 30'. Which choice matches that exact order?

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.1) Which equation represents: 'Seven less than a number is 18'?
approaching.explanation: 'Seven less than a number' means start with the number and subtract 7: n − 7 = 18.
choiceFeedback: Start with the variable, then subtract — not the other way.
The clue says "fewer" or "less" — use subtraction, not addition.
Use subtraction for "fewer" or "less," not division.
hints: 'Seven less than a number' is tricky — the number comes FIRST, and then 7 is taken away from it.
'Less than' flips the wording: '7 less than n' means start at n and subtract 7, not start at 7 and subtract n.
Write the number first: n, then subtract 7, then set it equal to 18. Which choice is built in that order?

approaching.explanation: Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9 = 6. Check: 6 + 9 = 15 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: x has 9 added to it. To get x alone, you need to UNDO that addition.
Use the inverse operation: subtraction undoes addition. Whatever you do, do it to BOTH sides to keep the balance.
Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9. Then check by adding 9 back to your result — do you land on 15?

approaching.explanation: Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7 = 27. Check: 27 − 7 = 20 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: Look at what's happening to y: 7 is being SUBTRACTED. Which operation undoes subtraction?
Add the same amount to both sides so the equation stays balanced and y ends up alone.
Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7. Check your result: does it minus 7 give back 20?

approaching.explanation: Divide both sides by 6: x = 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Check: 6 × 7 = 42 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: 6x means 6 TIMES x — the variable is being multiplied by 6.
Division undoes multiplication. Divide both sides by 6 to leave x alone.
Compute 42 ÷ 6, then check by multiplying your answer by 6 — do you get 42 back?

approaching.explanation: Multiply both sides by 3: n = 8 × 3 = 24. Check: 24 / 3 = 8 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: n is being DIVIDED by 3. Which operation undoes division?
Multiply both sides by 3 — the ÷3 and ×3 cancel each other, leaving just n.
Compute 8 × 3, then check: your answer divided by 3 should give 8.

onLevel.label: (Lesson 7.1) Match each situation to its equation

pairs.situation: A detective has some cases. After getting 9 new cases, she has 22.
A suspect's age divided by 3 equals 12.
Four times the number of fingerprints equals 28.
A detective had some clues. After removing 6, she had 15 left.

onLevel.hint: Read each item carefully, then match based on what the problem is asking.
hints: Underline the action in each situation: 'getting 9 new', 'divided by 3', 'four times', 'removing 6'. Each one names a single operation.
Match operations first: getting more means +, removing means −, 'times' means ×, 'divided' means /. Then check that the numbers agree too.
Try the first one: she has some cases (n) and GETS 9 more to reach 22 total. That is n plus something equals 22 — find the equation shaped that way.

rows.situation: A box holds some files. After removing 5, there are 13 left.
rows.variable: Number of files in the box

rows.situation: A detective split 48 photos equally into folders. Each folder has 6 photos.

onLevel.label: (Lesson 7.1) For each situation, identify what the variable represents and write the equation.
onLevel.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: Row 1: the box starts with an unknown number of files — that unknown starting amount is exactly what n stands for.
Ask two questions for each row: What number don't we know? (that's n) What happened to it? (5 removed, or 48 photos split equally).
Row 1: removing 5 files is subtraction, and 13 remain — so write n, minus 5, equals 13. Then set up row 2 the same careful way.

onLevel.label: (Lesson 7.2) Solve: m − 14 = 32
hints: The inverse of subtracting 14 is adding 14.
Add 14 to both sides: m = 32 + 14 = 46.

onLevel.label: (Lesson 7.2) Complete the table: identify the inverse operation, solve, and check.
onLevel.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: Every row asks the same three things: what is being done to the variable, how do you undo it, and does the check rebuild the original equation?
If the equation ADDS a number, the inverse is subtract; if it SUBTRACTS, the inverse is add. Always do it to both sides — decimals like 3.5 follow the same rule.
Row 1: x + 18 = 45 adds 18, so subtract 18 from both sides and compute 45 − 18. Verify by adding 18 back, then move to row 2.

onLevel.label: (Lesson 7.3) Solve each equation, show your work, and check.
onLevel.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: First decide for each row: is the variable being MULTIPLIED (like 8m) or DIVIDED (like y / 6)?
Use the inverse: divide both sides when the equation multiplies; multiply both sides when it divides. The Check column rebuilds the original.
Row 1: 8m = 56 multiplies by 8, so compute 56 ÷ 8 for m. Check it by multiplying back, then handle y / 6 = 11 with the opposite move.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.3) A detective splits 54 clues equally among 9 case files. The equation 9c = 54 represents this. What is c?
onLevel.explanation: Divide both sides by 9: c = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 clues per file.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: c is the number of clues in EACH file, and 9 files with c clues each make all 54 clues.
9c = 54 multiplies c by 9 — undo it by dividing both sides by 9, not by adding or subtracting.
Compute 54 ÷ 9 (what times 9 makes 54?). Your answer should be much smaller than 54 — clues per file, not the total.

extending.title: (Lesson 7.1) Find the Equation Error
extending.correctWork: 'Twice' means multiply by 2, not add 2. The correct equation is 2n = 16.
hints: What does 'twice' really mean — adding or multiplying?
'Twice a number' means 2 times the number, so the equation is 2n = 16.

extending.title: (Lesson 7.2) Find the Equation Error
extending.correctWork: Inverse of subtraction is ADDITION. Add 18 to both sides: x = 45 + 18 = 63.
hints: Step 2 says the inverse of subtraction is subtraction. Is that right?
To undo −18, you need +18, not another −18. Addition undoes subtraction.

extending.title: (Lesson 7.3) Find the Equation Error
extending.correctWork: Inverse of division is MULTIPLICATION. Multiply both sides by 5: x = 12 × 5 = 60. Check: 60 / 5 = 12 ✓
hints: Step 2 says the inverse of division is division. Is that correct?
To undo ÷ 5, you need × 5. Multiplication undoes division.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Solve Multiplication and Division Equations is applying the SAME operation again instead of the inverse — for example, seeing 6x = 42 and multiplying both sides by 6 to get x = 252, instead of dividing by 6 to get x = 7. Before you submit, ask: did I use the OPPOSITE operation shown in the equation, and did I apply it to both sides?

diagram.title: Splitting the $63 Kit Bill
diagram.caption: The top bar is the whole bill ($63); below it we split it into equal $7 groups — counting the 9 groups shows k = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 kits.

connect.scenario: A detective ordered fingerprint kits for her team. Each kit costs $7, and the total bill was $63. The equation 7k = 63 represents this situation, where k is the number of kits.
connect.promptQuestion: How many kits did the detective order? How did inverse operations help you solve this?
connect.prompt: The detective ordered ___ kits because 7k = 63 means k = 63 ÷ ___ = ___.

exitTicket.explanation: Subtract 2.8 from both sides: p = 9.1 − 2.8 = 6.3. Check: 6.3 + 2.8 = 9.1 ✓ (11.9 comes from adding instead of subtracting; 7.7 comes from subtracting each decimal place without regrouping — 9 − 2 = 7 and, without borrowing, 8 − 1 = 7; 3.25 comes from dividing 9.1 ÷ 2.8 instead of subtracting.)
choiceFeedback: You added 2.8 — undo it by subtracting from both sides.
Recheck your subtraction: 9.1 − 2.8 in the tenths place.
Subtract 2.8 from 9.1 — that's not the result.
hints: p has 2.8 added to it. To get p alone you must undo the addition — decimals follow the same rule as whole numbers.
Subtract 2.8 from both sides. Line up the decimal points and watch the tenths place for regrouping.
Set up 9.1 − 2.8: you can't take 8 tenths from 1 tenth, so borrow from the 9 first. Then check by adding 2.8 back to your result.
